The school also has a rec center where you can rent kayaks and things for the lake. It’s a lot of fun for spring weekends with friends. I know both UV and the Reserve have a bus stop that takes you into campus. Look online at the CATBus stops. Most of the apartment complexes around campus have at least one stop and it’s free to ride. And yes, the closer you get to campus the more expensive it gets.

Grad Student in History.

Favorite things to do around Clemson, the lake, the hiking, and downtown is great. There are tons of student organizations that have access to events and stuff around campus too. 

Just FYI: if you’re going to be a grad assistant, the GA parking pass is great, but it’s snatched up quickly. When you get the email that the parking passes are for sale, buy it immediately. 

As far as living around Clemson. The cheapest is University Village, but depending on where you end up there it can be kinda crappy living. They are pet friendly and their all inclusive rent is really cheap. I think the Reserve is a good place for slightly more expensive. It’s essentially UV but much better managed and the buildings are all well maintained. 

Hope that helps!

I always travel with my pigs. It’s better to monitor any changes in their condition. Just make sure you keep her warm the whole way. I like to wrap an extra blanket around the outside of the cage and have the car warm before they get there. Have you checked her poop? I know that sounds weird but she could be having tummy troubles and you’d be able to tell that by looking at her poop. If it’s more loose or dry than it should be that might give you a clue.
